fieldMarks: Largest deer; up to almost 1.8 m at the shoulder, with a humped shoulder and low rump
Long mournful arched nose with a flexible upper lip; most have a fur-covered 'bell' hanging from the throat
Dark brown to nearly black, reddish or grayish brown with pale gray or white leg 'stockings'
Only bulls carry antlers: broad palms fringed with spikes, grown each summer
behavior: Rut in late September–early October; cows bawl nasally and bulls answer with a coughing bellow
Browses willow, birch and aspen twigs in fall and winter, sometimes leaving a browse line 1.8–2.4 m high; feeds on aquatic plants in summer
Makes seasonal movements of a few to about 100 km between calving, rutting and wintering areas
Cools off in water in summer and may dive for bottom plants
habitat: A mosaic of second-growth forest, openings, swamps, lakes and wetlands; needs water for summer foraging and hardwood-conifer forest for winter cover; recent burns with dense willow, aspen and birch are prime.
range: Across the northern forests of North America from Alaska and Canada south into the Rocky Mountains and the northern United States; introduced to Newfoundland and Colorado.
